name: r1t6
diagnosis: Current FDIR allows one latch. It often latches a first mildly-degraded friction wheel (severity 0.2, residual ~3-5e-04 Nm) then cannot address a later severe wheel, leaving the severe wheel in the 3-wheel allocation causing policy-induced attitude loss/saturation. Open swap was meant to fix ordering but swaps similarly-degraded wheels, changing geometry and destabilizing control.
rationale: Narrow swap to clearly-dead replaces clearly-mild only. Re-enable allowed only if recorded residual <=0.0004 Nm (mild) and new residual >=0.002 Nm with ratio >=5. This targets mild-first/severe-second ordering that dominates rw_friction+rw_friction attitude loss, keeps 3-wheel control on healthiest wheels, and ignores comparable-degradation cases where swap was harmful.
why_no_regressions: All three listed regressions blocked: case1 old 5.11e-04>0.0004 and ratio 3.9<5; case2 old 5.74e-04>0.0004; case3 new 1.14e-03<0.002 and ratio 3.56<5. Strictly narrower than try5, so fewer triggers.
gate_reason: rejected: 3 new violations in 3 runs (3 previously clean) (evaluation stopped early after 25 runs)
sat_rule_recheck: 2026-11-04: re-decided on the consecutive-rule-corrected suite (data/satfix/gates_corrected.json); decision unchanged
